clue.text: After a premonition put money on one who is crooked

indicators.note: the money-staking piece is placed after the premonition piece in the answer

parts.note: a premonition is a hunch, a gut feeling about what will happen
to back a horse is to put money on it

explanation.surface: Acting on a gut feeling, a gambler bets on a dishonest character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the betting word follows the premonition. 'Crooked' here means bent in the back, not dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a curved spine, bent over, is literally crooked in posture.

clue.text: Not just biased

definitions.meaning: not just means lacking in fairness or justice
biased means prejudiced, favouring one side

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is partial rather than fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not just lacks fairness, and a biased judgement shows partiality; both describe injustice.

clue.text: Priest from the Magic Circle!

indicators.note: magic transforms things, so the letters of the following word are conjured into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns out to be a member of the conjurors' society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is the British society of professional magicians; here 'Magic' rearranges the letters of 'Circle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, and a priest is one such churchman.

clue.text: Anything large found on the motor car?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means exceptionally big, as in a ... harvest
the shock-absorbing bar fixed to the front and back of a vehicle

explanation.surface: A question about what big thing might be fitted to an automobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper is something unusually large (a bumper crop) and also the protective bar at a car's front and rear.

clue.text: Dead skin having been cut I cleaned some of it

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up the trimmed skin around a fingernail after cutting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the layer of hardened, dead tissue at the base of a fingernail.

clue.text: Explain how one should record one's vote

definitions.meaning: to communicate an idea successfully to listeners

definitions.text: how one should record one's vote
definitions.meaning: read as three words, it says to place an X on the ballot

explanation.surface: Instructions for how to mark a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea over is to explain it; on a ballot paper a voter marks an X beside their choice.

clue.text: African has very warm shelter to enter

parts.note: hot means very warm

indicators.note: the small word is made to go into the shelter word, entering it

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa owns a sweltering hut they must go into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts TO inside TENT, between its N and final T, giving TENTOT. The word is an old, now offensive name for the Khoikhoi people.
explanation.definitionFit: The term historically named a pastoral people of south-western Africa, the Khoikhoi.

clue.text: Powerful attack-but not at the front of the ship

definitions.meaning: a forceful critical onslaught, from a ship firing all guns on one side

definitions.text: not at the front of the ship
definitions.meaning: the flank of a vessel, rather than its bow

explanation.surface: A naval battle in which a ship fires on another from its flank.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal or written assault, and also the whole side of a vessel above the waterline.

clue.text: Indulge hesitantly in time

indicators.note: the hesitating sound sits within the time word

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
um is the noise a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Giving in to someone's whims slowly and with pauses, in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hesitantly' gives UM, the sound of someone pausing, which goes inside HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to go along with their wishes to keep them content, which is indulging them.

clue.text: Second crop of grass cultivated at the farm

indicators.note: land that is cultivated is worked over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer grows a further harvest of grass in a tilled field.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday sense of the answer is the consequences of a disaster; its original farming sense, a second mowing, is what the clue uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a farming term for the new growth of grass mown after the first cut.

clue.text: Girl to ruin fancy hat

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: fancy as a verb of imagining suggests letters reworked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A young woman wrecks an elaborate hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective describing the hat, but it rearranges HAT to THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Stage-coach industry

definitions.meaning: a public passenger coach in France and Europe
industry in the sense of hard work and application

explanation.surface: A transport business running horse-drawn carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligence was a public stagecoach in France; diligence is also hard-working effort.

clue.text: Marks or trademarks

definitions.meaning: marks burned onto cattle or other things

explanation.surface: Labels placed on goods to show who made them.
explanation.definitionFit: Brands are marks burned into livestock and also the names under which companies sell products.

clue.text: Frequently said to be one composer or another

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, its pronunciation giving the first part

parts.note: frequently means often, which some speakers pronounce with a silent t
another composer is Bach, the German Baroque master

explanation.surface: Someone is often said to be one music-writer or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' asks for the sound of OFTEN with its T silent, OFFEN; BACH, another composer, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was a 19th-century composer of French operettas, including Orpheus in the Underworld.

clue.text: One who attacks mad alsatians

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so the dog breed's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Crazed guard dogs turning on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian is the British name for a German Shepherd dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, someone who sets upon another person.

clue.text: A novice in one country or another

indicators.note: the letter and the novice go within the first country

parts.note: Austria is a country in central Europe
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A beginner living in one nation or perhaps a different nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L (the learner driver's plate) go inside AUSTRIA, between its R and I. 'another' then defines, short for another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a further nation, distinct from Austria, so 'another' country fits.

clue.text: Although not at home start to ask earnestly

indicators.note: not means the home word is left out of the start word

parts.note: to begin is to start
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Even though they are out, someone begins to make an urgent request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' looks like 'begin to', but it is BEGIN, which loses IN (at home).
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead or entreat someone urgently.

clue.text: We will all retire to it soon or later

definitions.text: We will all retire to it soon or later

parts.words: We will all retire to it soon or later
parts.note: sounds like a remark about death or leaving work, but means the place everyone goes when going to sleep

explanation.surface: A gloomy reflection that everyone eventually stops working or dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring at night means going to sleep, which people do on a mattress-topped frame.

clue.text: This joke will silence one

definitions.meaning: a cloth tied over the mouth stops someone speaking

explanation.surface: A wisecrack that shuts a heckler up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a comedian's quip, and also a cloth tied over someone's mouth to stop them speaking.

clue.text: Start of fault is certain to produce a crack

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A geological fault is guaranteed to open up a gap in the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' looks like the geology word, but only its first letter, F, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow opening or split in rock or tissue.

clue.text: Go without saying

parts.note: the idiom for being obvious, reread as leaving without saying goodbye

explanation.surface: Something too obvious to need stating.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to slip away secretly, leaving without telling anyone.

clue.text: Approve of what gardeners sometimes do

definitions.meaning: slang for to like or appreciate
gardeners turn over soil with a spade

explanation.surface: Gardeners enjoy their work in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something is slang for liking it; gardeners also turn the soil with a spade.

clue.text: Four leave calm situation offering no escape

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for four departs from the calm word

parts.note: impassive means calm, showing no emotion
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people walk out of a tranquil situation that turns out to be a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four leave' takes IV, the Roman numeral for four, out of IMPASSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a position from which there is no way forward.

clue.text: Vehicle in summer in France for a card game

indicators.note: the vehicle sits inside the French summer word

parts.note: été is French for summer
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car trip during a French summer for a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a French card game for two players, using a thirty-two-card pack.

clue.text: The initial mistake causes great fear

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: An early blunder leads to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fright or dread.

clue.text: Straps Heather on board

indicators.note: with board this reads on board, being inside a ship, so the plant goes inside

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS stands for steamship
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: Bundles of heather tied down with belts on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board means inside a ship, written SS (steamship), so LING goes inside SS. Ling is a common heather of British moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Slings are straps or loops used to support or carry something, such as an injured arm.

clue.text: Prevail on Italian dictator I name first

indicators.note: the letter and the name come first, before the dictator

parts.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, the Italian dictator

explanation.surface: Persuading Mussolini, someone puts their own name forward first.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini was known as Il Duce, 'the leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade them, to prevail on them to act.

clue.text: Attractive calling of men in the field

definitions.text: calling of men in the field
definitions.meaning: in cricket, fielders shout to the umpire claiming a batsman is out

explanation.surface: Fielders' cries can be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders appeal by shouting 'Howzat?' to ask the umpire to give the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means pleasing; in cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire by shouting for a batsman to be given out.

clue.text: Everything in unpleasant but sentimental song

indicators.note: the totality word is placed inside the unpleasant word

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
all means everything

explanation.surface: A song that is mawkish and generally not much good.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a slow, romantic or sentimental popular song.

clue.text: Does he get a rocket for travelling whilst at work?

definitions.text: Does he get a rocket for travelling whilst at work?

parts.words: Does he get a rocket for travelling whilst at work?
parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a telling-off, but here it is a spacecraft that carries this worker

explanation.surface: An employee is reprimanded for travelling on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: To get a rocket is British slang for being severely told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller's job involves riding a rocket into orbit.

clue.text: Frank is able to have performed

parts.note: can means is able
did means carried out or performed

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is capable of having acted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means open and honest in speech.

clue.text: The newspapers indeed are gloomy

indicators.note: the newspapers go inside the act word

parts.note: a deed is an act
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Journalists really are downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in' and 'deed': PRESS goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed means low in spirits, dejected.
